description: Patients qualify only if one laboratory record shows both a urine protein result of '-' and a rheumatoid factor result of '-'.

d.request: Among patients having at least one single laboratory record where `U-PRO` = '-' and `RA` = '-' simultaneously, compute each such patient's average `PT` and average of (`TAT` − `TAT2`) over all of their laboratory records (ignoring NULLs), then return the average of the per-patient PT averages and the average of the per-patient TAT − TAT2 averages as one unrounded row.
d.sql: SELECT AVG(avg_pt) AS avg_pt, AVG(avg_diff) AS avg_tat_diff FROM (SELECT ID, AVG(PT) AS avg_pt, AVG(TAT - TAT2) AS avg_diff FROM Laboratory WHERE ID IN (SELECT ID FROM Laboratory WHERE `U-PRO` = '-' AND RA = '-') GROUP BY ID)

b.request: Select patients having at least one single Laboratory record where `U-PRO` = '-' and `RA` = '-' simultaneously, then using all of each such patient's Laboratory records compute the per-patient average `PT` and average of (`TAT` − `TAT2`) ignoring NULLs, and return one row with the unrounded average of the per-patient PT averages and the average of the per-patient TAT − TAT2 averages.
b.sql: WITH p AS (SELECT DISTINCT ID FROM Laboratory WHERE `U-PRO` = '-' AND RA = '-'), per AS (SELECT l.ID, AVG(l.PT) AS avg_pt, AVG(l.TAT - l.TAT2) AS avg_diff FROM Laboratory l JOIN p ON p.ID = l.ID GROUP BY l.ID) SELECT AVG(avg_pt) AS avg_pt, AVG(avg_diff) AS avg_tat_diff FROM per
b.raw: Select patients having at least one single Laboratory record where `U-PRO` = '-' and `RA` = '-' simultaneously, then using all of each such patient's Laboratory records compute the per-patient average `PT` and average of (`TAT` − `TAT2`) ignoring NULLs, and return one row with the unrounded average of the per-patient PT averages and the average of the per-patient TAT − TAT2 averages.

c.request: Consider patients whose laboratory results include a urine protein (`U-PRO`) result of exactly '-' and a rheumatoid factor (`RA`) result of exactly '-'. For each such patient, use all of their laboratory records to compute the average prothrombin time (`PT`) and the average of `TAT` minus `TAT2`. Across these patients, what are the average of the per-patient PT averages and the average of the per-patient TAT − TAT2 averages? Give them as a single row with these two values, unrounded, and ignore missing values at every step. Patients qualify only if one laboratory record shows both a urine protein result of '-' and a rheumatoid factor result of '-'.
c.sql: WITH q AS (SELECT DISTINCT ID FROM Laboratory WHERE `U-PRO` = '-' AND RA = '-'), per AS (SELECT l.ID, AVG(l.PT) AS avg_pt, AVG(l.TAT - l.TAT2) AS avg_diff FROM Laboratory l JOIN q ON q.ID = l.ID GROUP BY l.ID) SELECT AVG(avg_pt) AS avg_pt, AVG(avg_diff) AS avg_tat_diff FROM per

a.request: Consider patients who have at least one laboratory record on which the urine protein (`U-PRO`) result is exactly '-' and the rheumatoid factor (`RA`) result is also exactly '-'. For each such patient, use all of their laboratory records to compute the average prothrombin time (`PT`) and the average of `TAT` minus `TAT2`. Across these patients, what are the average of the per-patient PT averages and the average of the per-patient TAT − TAT2 averages? Give them as a single row with these two values, unrounded, and ignore missing values at every step.
a.sql: WITH qualifying AS (SELECT DISTINCT ID FROM Laboratory WHERE `U-PRO` = '-' AND RA = '-'), per_patient AS (SELECT l.ID, AVG(l.PT) AS avg_pt, AVG(l.TAT - l.TAT2) AS avg_tat_diff FROM Laboratory l JOIN qualifying q ON l.ID = q.ID GROUP BY l.ID) SELECT AVG(avg_pt) AS avg_of_avg_pt, AVG(avg_tat_diff) AS avg_of_avg_tat_diff FROM per_patient
